What the card brings is visibility. A pay rise other people hear about, a sale that goes well, being paid properly for something you're known for. Jupiter is generous and so is Leo, and together they'd like the money to show. The square is where it rubs. Taurus wants money that sits quietly and grows, and this card wants to spend some of it where people can see, the round of drinks, the car, the dinner where you grab the bill. Both can be fine. The friction is in noticing which one you're doing and why, and to be honest most people with this card in the second are a little more tempted to show off than they'd admit.

In your income it's the moment to ask for more, especially if your work has recently been noticed. In spending it's the generous gesture, which is lovely when you can afford it. In self-worth it's feeling for once that you've earned your place. Put a figure on what your work is worth and say it to whoever pays you.
2.reversed:
The second house with the Six reversed can end up paying for the look of success. Money goes on things that tell people you're doing well, and the account behind them is thinner than anyone knows. Jupiter makes it all feel affordable in the moment, and Leo's pride makes it hard to scale back once you've been seen living a certain way. The fixed square digs in on both. Or it goes quieter, and your sense of your own worth rises and falls with whether anyone praised you lately.

Look at the credit card statement and the purchase you'd be embarrassed to explain. Look at work, too, where you might be underpaid and too proud to raise it, because raising it means admitting it. Venus rules this house and has good taste, which includes knowing what's worth the money. Go through a month of spending and circle everything you bought mostly for someone else to see.

3.upright:
Everyday talk belongs to the third house. The emails, the group chat, the sibling you ring on Sundays, the neighbour over the fence, the short drives, the things you pick up by reading. It's cadent, a learning house, with Gemini as its natural sign and Mercury as its ruler, and the Moon has its joy here. Leo sits two signs from Gemini, a sextile, and fire and air get on well, so on the surface this is an easy fit and the card finds its voice quickly.

The snag is Jupiter. It's in detriment in Gemini, the sign opposite its own, and this house is Gemini's by nature, so the card's planet is working against the grain. Jupiter likes the big statement, the speech, the one story told well. This house likes quick, accurate back-and-forth, and it notices when someone's holding the floor. What you might find is that people are listening to you more, which feels good, and that you've started talking in announcements. The message that's a paragraph too long. The meeting where you explained what everyone already knew. The warmth is real and people like it. They'd just like a turn as well.

With a brother or sister it can bring a proud moment, you celebrating their win or them celebrating yours, and now and then a flash of old rivalry about who's doing better. In learning it helps with presenting, teaching, putting your writing out. Around the neighbourhood it's being known by name. In the next group conversation you're in, count how many questions you ask.
3.reversed:
Turned over in the third house, the Six has talk working for applause. The story gets a little bigger each time you tell it, the point gets made loudly so people see you make it, and you're three sentences into correcting someone before you've checked you're right. Jupiter already struggles in this house's Gemini nature, and upside down it inflates the words past what's behind them. Fire and air catch quickly, so the exaggeration travels.

Siblings feel it, where old competition over who's the clever one or the successful one can flare up about something small. Colleagues feel it in your messages and meetings, and start trusting your numbers a little less. Learning suffers when you sound surer of a subject than you are. Mercury, the house's ruler, is fussy about accuracy. Next time you catch yourself rounding a story up, go back and give the real size of it.

4.upright:
Home is the fourth house. The actual house or flat, the family you grew up in and the one you've made, and the private life that goes on behind the front door. It's angular, the bottom corner of the chart, and Cancer's by nature, with the Moon as ruler. Jupiter is exalted in Cancer, so this card's planet is a very welcome guest here. There's a lot of warmth on offer.

The friction is in the elements. The Six is fire and a public card, a parade down the main street, and this house is water and wants its privacy. Leo and Cancer sit side by side in the zodiac and have very little in common. So you may feel pulled between wanting the home to be something you show, the renovation, the dinner party, the family that looks good in photos, and wanting it to be the one place nobody's watching and you can take your shoes off. The exaltation means both are possible. The good version is a home people love coming to that still feels like yours once they've gone. I've seen this card in the fourth turn up around a family celebration, a parent's big birthday, a graduation, somebody at home being proud of you out loud.

With family it can be the recognition you wanted from a parent, finally said. With the house itself it's pride in the place, maybe a long project finished. With the people you live with it's being valued for what you do at home, which usually goes unnoticed. Have people over, then keep the next night free for just the household.
4.reversed:
When the Six is upside down in the fourth, home can turn into somewhere you perform. The house is kept for how it looks to visitors, the family story gets told at its best, and underneath something hasn't been said for a long time. Jupiter is still exalted here, so the warmth is really there, but fire and water make steam, and the tension tends to sit in the kitchen where everyone can feel it and nobody names it.

Parents are often part of it, especially one whose approval you've been chasing for years. So is the house, with money spent on the front rooms while the bedroom's a mess, and a partner or kids who'd like more of you and less of the hosting. The Moon rules this house and needs feeding quietly. Cook a plain meal for the people you live with and sit down to eat it with them, phones in another room.

5.upright:
This is the Six's own house. The fifth is play, romance, children, hobbies, the thing you make for the fun of it, and any stage you get up on. It's Leo's house by nature, ruled by the Sun, and Venus has its joy here. The card lives in Leo, so drawing it into the fifth puts it on its own ground, fire meeting fire in the house it was built for.

Something you've made gets an audience, or a romance goes public, or a child does something that makes you burst with pride. Jupiter enlarges all of it, and Venus, happy in this house, adds plain pleasure. The only thing to watch comes with the amplifying, because the same element turns up the too much along with the good. Once a hobby starts getting praised it can turn into a performance without you noticing, and suddenly you're checking the likes on a photo of the cake you baked for fun. Love works the same way. It's lovely being seen as a couple, and it's easy to start dating for the story you'll tell about it.

In creative work it's the gig, the exhibition, the post that goes further than you expected. In romance it's being claimed in public, the introduction to friends, the photo together. With children it's their win, and the chance to let it stay theirs. Keep one hobby completely private, and make something with it that nobody else will ever see.
5.reversed:
The Six upside down in the fifth can turn fun into hard work. Even on home ground the doubled fire can overheat, and the joy starts to depend on who's watching. The song you wrote sounds worse because nobody commented. The date was fine, but you spent half of it working out how it would sound when you told your friends. Jupiter reversed tends to overdo things, and here what it overdoes is the need for a reaction.

Creative work stalls because you've started making it for an audience you haven't got yet. A partner can tell when they're being shown off. With children, their achievement quietly becomes yours. Venus has its joy in this house and likes pleasure for its own sake. Pick up something you used to do badly and happily as a kid, and do it badly again for an afternoon.

6.upright:
Nobody claps for the dishes, and the sixth house is mostly dishes. It's the ordinary working day, the commute, the inbox, the gym bag by the door, the body's upkeep and the small habits that keep everything running. It's cadent, a house of service and adjustment, with Virgo as its natural sign and Mercury as its ruler, and Mars has its joy here. Leo and Virgo are neighbours with little in common, and the card's fire has no natural feeling for this house's earth, so the Six arrives as a bit of a stranger.

Jupiter is in detriment in Virgo, and that decides a lot. Jupiter is a big-picture planet and this house is all detail, the same walk every morning, the tidy spreadsheet, ten minutes of stretching before bed. So the card's wish for a visible win meets a house where the wins are small and pile up slowly, and you may feel impatient with it. You want the transformation and the house wants you to floss. The good version is some real recognition at work for the reliable stuff, the thing you do every day that nobody normally mentions, and a bit of pride in your own routine. Mars likes effort in this house, which helps.

At work it can be a manager finally noticing the quiet jobs, or a small award. In the body it's measurable progress, a faster run, a heavier lift, better sleep. In the daily routine it's getting some pleasure back into the chores. Pick one small daily habit and keep a tally on the fridge of the days you do it.
6.reversed:
Reversed in the sixth, the Six can have you looking well while running low. You're at the gym for the photo, or answering emails at eleven at night so nobody can say you're slacking, and the body keeps quiet about it for a while. Jupiter in detriment here, and upside down, tends to overreach, so the plan is always the big one, the six-day program, the whole new diet, and it's collapsed by the second week.

At work it looks like overcommitting to be seen as the reliable one and then resenting the load. In the body it's tiredness covered over with caffeine and pride. With colleagues it's wanting credit for the dull work when nobody's handing it out. Mercury rules this house and likes small steps. Drop the big plan, choose the smallest version of it, and do only that.

7.upright:
The seventh house is the person opposite. A partner, a business partner, the client you sign with, sometimes the rival you keep measuring yourself against. It's angular and very visible. Libra is its natural sign and Venus its ruler. Leo is two signs from Libra, a sextile, and fire and air feed each other, so the card is welcome here and things between two people tend to move quickly.

What it brings is pride in each other. You might be in a stretch where your partner is openly glad to be with you, telling their friends, turning up to your thing, and you're doing the same back. Or a working partnership gets noticed and the two of you become known as a team. Jupiter makes it generous. A sextile is an opening that still has to be taken, though. Somebody has to say the proud thing out loud, and in a lot of couples each person assumes the other already knows. Leo's pride can get in the way as well, if one of you is quietly keeping score of who's being celebrated more.

With a partner it suits a public step, meeting the family, moving in, an engagement, or just a proper night out together. In business it's a partnership that looks good and does well. With contracts it's a fair deal both sides can be pleased with. Tell your partner, specifically, one thing they did that you were proud of.
7.reversed:
Upside down in the seventh, the Six can leave a relationship leaning on how it looks. One of you does the admiring and the other soaks it up, or the two of you are great at parties and a bit flat at home. Sometimes it's rivalry, a partner whose success you ought to be happy about and aren't quite. Fire and air move fast, so these patterns settle in quicker than you'd think.

Between partners it's the photo that says one thing and the drive home that says another. In business it's a partnership where one person gets all the credit and the other has started to mind. With a contract it's the deal that sounded better in the meeting. Venus rules this house and wants things even. Ask your partner, or the person you work with, whether they feel appreciated, and then listen without explaining yourself.

8.upright:
A rider going through a cheering crowd is about as public as a card gets, and the eighth house is the most private room in the chart. Joint money, debt, the mortgage, an inheritance, sex and the trust that goes with it, and the endings that change you. It's succedent, with Scorpio as its natural sign and Mars as its traditional ruler, Pluto its modern one. Leo squares Scorpio, fixed against fixed, and fire and water are opposed elements, so there's real friction here.

What this pairing often asks for is some of the Six's confidence in places you'd usually go quiet. Saying what you want in bed. Saying what you earn to the person you're combining finances with. Telling people plainly that something has ended. It can be a genuinely good time to sort out shared money, since Jupiter is generous and the confidence helps with an awkward conversation. The square is felt when pride gets in the way, when you'd sooner look fine than admit to a debt, or you keep a good face on in the middle of a loss because falling apart would be seen.

In shared finances the card favours a settlement, a loan approved, a fair split after a separation. In intimacy it's warmth and being wanted, and saying so. With an ending it's letting people see you grieve. Sit down with whoever you share money with and write every account and every debt on one page.
8.reversed:
The Six reversed in the eighth tends to keep a good face on over something deep. A debt you haven't mentioned, a loss you're getting through by being busy and cheerful, a closeness that's become a bit of a performance. Fire and water under a fixed square build pressure with nowhere to go, and Jupiter upside down makes the front bigger. Pride is usually the reason. Admitting the thing would mean looking less like you've got it handled.

Joint finances are the obvious place, where one person's spending or earning has become a sore subject nobody raises. Sex is another, where confidence has turned into something you act. Then there's the ending, a breakup or a death, where you've been strong for everyone for a long time. Mars is the traditional ruler of this house and respects honesty, even the blunt kind. Tell one person the true number, or the true feeling, and let them see it.

9.upright:
The ninth house is the long view. Study, travel, belief, publishing, the law, and whatever you think a life is for. It's cadent, a house of learning. Sagittarius is its natural sign, and Jupiter, the Six's own planet, is its ruler, so the card is standing on home ground. Leo trines Sagittarius, fire to fire, and the Sun has its joy here too. Everything in this pairing pulls in one direction.

That makes it one of the strongest houses for the card. What it tends to look like is recognition for what you know. A course finished with a certificate at the end, a piece of writing accepted, a talk that goes well, being asked for your view because people trust it. Travel can come into it, a trip that feels like a reward, or work sending you somewhere far. Jupiter at home is generous and the confidence is well founded. The amplifying is the only catch. With fire on fire and Jupiter in charge you can end up very sure of yourself, and a bit preachy about whatever just worked for you. I'd keep an eye on that at family dinners.

In study it backs applying, graduating, publishing. In travel it's the trip you've been talking about for years. In belief it's feeling that the way you live makes sense to you. Book the course, or the ticket, and tell someone you've done it.
9.reversed:
With the Six turned over in the ninth, belief gets loud. You're sure you're right about something, politics, a diet, how to raise kids, how business works, and the certainty is doing the job curiosity used to do. Jupiter is strong here on home ground, so when it tips over it tips over a long way. The doubled fire keeps the whole thing convincing, mostly to you.

In study it's confidence running ahead of what you actually know, or a course dropped because it stopped flattering you. In travel it's the big trip planned on enthusiasm, with the visa sorted at the last minute. At the dinner table it's an argument you don't need to win. Jupiter rules this house, and it's happiest learning something. Ask someone who disagrees with you to explain their view, and try repeating it back until they'd agree you've got it right.

10.upright:
The top of the chart is the tenth house. The career, the public role, what people say about you once you've left the room. It's angular, the most visible point there is. By nature it belongs to Capricorn and Saturn, and Jupiter is in fall in Capricorn, which matters. Leo and Capricorn are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, and fire and earth are strangers to each other. So a card that looks like recognition itself arrives in the house of recognition and finds the fit awkward.

The awkwardness is about pace. The Six wants the win seen, and Saturn's house hands out credit slowly, after years, once you've proved yourself. Jupiter in fall is uncomfortable and has to go the long way round, so the praise tends to come sideways. A mention in someone else's speech. A client who asks for you by name. The promotion that comes with more work and a smaller title than you hoped. I've seen a lot of people with this card in the tenth feel slightly let down by the size of the acknowledgement, and then find a year later that it held up better than a big fuss would have.

In your career it supports a step up, especially if you ask for it plainly. In reputation it's being known for something specific. With a boss it's being taken seriously at last. Write down three things you've done at work that you'd want on the record, and make sure the right person knows about them.
10.reversed:
The Six upside down in the tenth can leave you with a reputation bigger than the job underneath it. The title sounds good, the profile looks great, and privately you're worried someone will work out how much you're winging it. Or the credit for something you did went to someone else, and it still stings. Jupiter in fall is uneasy here already, and turned over it has you polishing the image when the work itself needs the hours.

With a manager it's the review where you oversold. With colleagues it's taking a bit more credit than you earned, or giving away yours. At parties it's the way you talk about your job. Saturn rules this house and respects work that's actually been done. Pick the part of your role you've been bluffing and put real hours into learning it.

11.upright:
Friends and groups are the eleventh house's business. The mates, the team, the online group, the club, and the hopes you carry for the next few years. It's succedent. Aquarius is its natural sign, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, and Jupiter has its joy here, which is good news for this card, because Jupiter does some of its best work in this house.

There's one tension. Leo sits opposite Aquarius, so the card's sign and the house's sign face each other across the chart, one person out front against the group. The Six is about a single rider being cheered, and the eleventh is about everyone being in it together. Fire and air are friendly, and with Jupiter happy here it usually works out, but you may notice some awkwardness about being singled out by people you think of as equals. Your friends throw you a party and you don't know where to look. The group wants you to lead it and you worry what that'll do to the friendships.

With friends it's being celebrated by your own people, a birthday, a win, a toast. In a group or team it's being put forward, maybe as captain or organiser. With your hopes it's a wish that suddenly has backing, someone who believes in it enough to help. Say yes to leading the thing, and when it goes well, hand out the thanks by name.
11.reversed:
The Six reversed in the eleventh can turn a friendship group into a scoreboard. Who's doing better, who got the invite, who liked the post and who didn't. Jupiter has its joy here and wants the whole circle lifted, and upside down that can shrink to wanting to be the most admired person in it. The Leo opposition pulls too far toward the one out front, and your friends feel it.

You might have started performing a bit with them, telling the good news louder and the bad news not at all. Networking turns into collecting people for how they look next to you. A hope for the future gets chosen for how it'll sound. Saturn is this house's traditional ruler and values loyalty that lasts. Ring the friend who's been having a hard time, ask about them, and keep your own news for another day.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the part of life that goes on offstage. Sleep, dreams, time alone, what you do that nobody sees, and the things about yourself you'd prefer not to look at. It's cadent. Pisces is its natural sign, Jupiter its traditional ruler with Neptune the modern one, and Saturn has its joy here. So Jupiter is on home turf and the blessing in this card is real. Leo and Pisces are quincunx, though, and fire and water are opposed, which makes this the oddest house of all for a card about being seen.

What usually happens is the Six turns inward. The win is private. You finished something nobody knew you'd started, or got through something hard without telling anyone, or you simply feel, on your own, that you've done alright. Jupiter looking after this house tends to show as help arriving from somewhere you didn't expect. The friction is that the card still wants a crowd, there isn't one, and some people find that surprisingly hard. There can be some doubt behind a good public face as well, a sneaking sense that you've fooled everyone.

In sleep it can show as better rest once a worry's settled. In time alone it's real pleasure in your own company. With work done behind the scenes it's help given without credit, and feeling fine about that. Do one kind thing for someone and make sure they never find out it was you.
12.reversed:
